title: The Math Behind Good Debt vs Bad Debt

beats.say: A $3,000 credit card balance can quietly trap your paycheck for 15 years.
beats.visual: Cinematic close-up of a worn leather wallet resting on a dark wooden table beside a pair of metal keys, moody dramatic lighting from a single lamp.

beats.say: At 24% APR, paying only the minimum burns $4,887 in interest over 183 months.
beats.visual: A hand holding an unbranded dark credit card over a dim mahogany desk, shallow depth of field, cool shadows.

beats.say: We're taught that all debt is financial suicide, so why do the wealthy borrow millions?
beats.visual: Silhouette of a person in a tailored coat looking out of a high-rise window at a sprawling metropolitan skyline at dusk.

beats.say: Most people assume the rich avoid borrowing, but they actually use debt as an acceleration engine.
beats.visual: Low-angle architectural shot of a massive stone financial institution with towering pillars, overcast gray sky.

beats.say: At 24% APR, bad debt doubles every 3 years. But how does 5x leverage actually work?
beats.visual: Close-up of an antique brass mechanical stopwatch ticking on a dark surface, cinematic side lighting.

beats.say: Put $20,000 down on a $100,000 property, and you control that entire asset with 5x leverage.
beats.visual: Cinematic wide exterior shot of a classic brick residential townhouse on a quiet street in late afternoon sun.

beats.say: A 20% rise in market value doubles your $20,000 down payment, before costs and interest.
beats.visual: Overhead cinematic shot of stacked architectural blueprints and brass measuring calipers on an oak drafting table.

beats.say: A 20% drop wipes out your $20,000 equity, and mortgage payments don't stop. So how do they survive?
beats.visual: A person viewed from behind standing under an umbrella in the pouring rain, watching mist roll over city rooftops.

beats.say: The wealthy only borrow when the asset's monthly cash flow covers both interest and principal payments.
beats.visual: Cinematic close-up of hands turning a heavy brass key in the solid lock of an apartment door.

beats.say: Consumer debt drains your own paycheck, while productive leverage forces an asset to build your wealth.
beats.visual: A pair of hands neatly aligning smooth wooden blocks on a minimalist concrete table, warm focused downlight.

beats.say: Never borrow for things that lose value. Use debt only when an asset repays the balance.
beats.visual: Cinematic side profile of a fountain pen resting on a heavy ledger book beside a cup of black coffee.

beats.say: Follow Quiet Money for the money rules school never taught you.
beats.visual: A silhouette walking calmly down an empty, grand hallway lined with tall windows and morning sunlight.

caption: Debt isn't inherently evil—it's a tool. Here is the exact math separating toxic consumer debt from productive leverage.
description: Most people view all debt as a financial trap, but the wealthy treat leverage as an acceleration tool. This video breaks down the mathematical difference between 24% revolving credit and 5x asset leverage.
first_comment: Are you currently carrying consumption debt or asset debt?

facts.claim: A $3,000 credit card at 24% APR paying only the minimum burns $4,887 in interest across 183 months.
facts.basis: Fact Sheet: $3,000 credit card at 24% APR paying only the minimum (1% + interest, min $25) takes 183 months and costs $4,887 in interest.

facts.claim: At 24% APR, debt doubles every 3 years under the Rule of 72.
facts.basis: Fact Sheet: Rule of 72: at 24% debt doubles every 3 years.

facts.claim: A $100,000 property bought with $20,000 down is 5x leverage; a 20% gain doubles equity while a 20% drop wipes it out before costs and interest.
facts.basis: Fact Sheet: Leverage math for a $100,000 property with $20,000 down.

loop_map.stakes: A $3,000 card balance can trap a paycheck in $4,887 of interest over 15 years.
loop_map.big_question: Why do the ultra-wealthy borrow millions if debt is supposed to be financial suicide?
loop_map.assume: All debt is dangerous and drains personal wealth.
loop_map.reveal: Productive leverage uses asset cash flow to repay the loan, while consumer debt drains personal paychecks.
